name: Mediator complex-related neurodevelopmental disorder
definition: A group of neurodevelopmental disorders caused by germline mutations in genes encoding subunits of the Mediator complex, a multi-protein assembly required for RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription. Shared phenotypic features include intellectual disability, speech and language delay, behavioral abnormalities, and variable structural brain anomalies.
grandparents: disease by developmental or physiological process
children_sample: cardiac anomalies - developmental delay - facial dysmorphism syndrome

name: P2RY12-related platelet disorder, autosomal dominant
definition: A platelet type bleeding disorder of autosomal dominant inheritance caused by a variation in the P2RY12 gene that exerts a dominant negative effect by disrupting receptor homodimerization, leading to markedly impaired adenosine diphosphate induced platelet aggregation despite normal receptor expression. Affected individuals may exhibit severe bleeding symptoms due to defective amplification of platelet activation signals.

name: GJB2-related disorder
definition: A genetic disorder caused by a variation in the GJB2 gene, primarily associated with hearing loss and/or deafness.
grandparents: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism

name: GP9-related Bernard-Soulier syndrome
definition: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome caused by the variation in the GP9 gene, marked by absent or markedly reduced GPIb-IX-V complex expression, resulting in impaired platelet adhesion and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Platelets are large and functionally deficient, with severely reduced ristocetin-induced agglutination reflecting loss of functional GPIX within the receptor complex. Variants in GP9 disrupt synthesis or stability of the GPIX subunit, preventing proper assembly of the GPIb-IX-V complex and producing the characteristic bleeding phenotype.

name: GP1BA-related Bernard-Soulier syndrome
definition: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the GP1BA gene, characterized by macrothrombocytopenia, reduced or absent expression of the GPIb-IX-V complex, and lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding. Affected individuals have large platelets with defective ristocetin-induced agglutination, reflecting the absence or dysfunction of GPIbα on the platelet surface. Variants in GP1BA impair production, trafficking, or incorporation of GPIbα into the receptor complex, preventing normal surface assembly and leading to the classic BSS adhesion defect.

name: GP1BB-related Bernard-Soulier syndrome
definition: Any Bernard-Soulier syndrome caused by deficiency or dysfunction of GPIbβ, leading to markedly decreased GPIb-IX-V surface expression and impaired platelet adhesion. Platelets are enlarged and poorly responsive to ristocetin, consistent with severe reduction of the assembled receptor complex. Variants in GP1BB affect production or proper folding of the GPIbβ subunit, preventing formation of the full receptor complex and resulting in the characteristic Bernard-Soulier phenotype.

name: AARS2-related disorder
definition: Any disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the AARS2 gene.
grandparents: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism

name: EDA-related ectodermal dysplasia
definition: Any ectodermal dysplasia syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the EDA gene. Key features are hypohidrosis and hypotrichosis; the condition is also characterized by skin anomalies such as soft, thin, and dry skin, eczema, and pigmentation anomalies, as well as fine or brittle hair, dental anomalies such as hypodontia or oligodontia, vocal hoarseness, and hyperthermia susceptibility.

name: THG1L-related disorder
definition: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, encompassing a phenotypic spectrum that ranges from mild cerebellar ataxia with developmental delay to severe epileptic encephalopathy.
grandparents: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism

name: THG1L-related epileptic encephalopathy
definition: Any genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in which the cause of the disease is a biallelic variation in the THG1L gene, characterized by profound developmental delay, microcephaly, intractable epilepsy, and cerebellar hypoplasia.

name: SCN2A-related disorder
definition: Any nervous system disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the SCN2A gene, which encodes the Nav1.2 sodium channel critical for neuronal function. SCN2A-related disorders span a broad phenotypic spectrum, from self-limited familial neonatal-infantile epilepsy through severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathies to later-onset epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability without seizures, and episodic ataxia. Because Nav1.2 is essential for brain development as well as neuronal excitability, the presentation is predominantly neurodevelopmental where developmental delay, intellectual disability, and autism spectrum disorder are the most consistent features across the spectrum, present even in the absence of seizures. Clinical severity is broadly associated with the functional effect of the variant on the Nav1.2 channel, with gain-of-function changes typically linked to early severe epilepsy and loss-of-function changes more often associated with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability or intellectual disability, although these relationships are complex and not fully understood.

name: EIF2B1-related permanent neonatal diabetes with transient liver dysfunction
synonyms: EIF2B1-related permanent neonatal diabetes with transient liver dysfunction
definition: Any permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the EIF2B1 gene, often accompanied by transient liver dysfunction.

name: IMPDH2-related disorder
related_synonyms: dominant juvenile-onset dystonia-tremor disorder due to IMPDH2 variants
definition: An ultra-rare hereditary neurological disorder caused by a variation in the IMPDH2 gene, which encodes a key enzyme involved in guanine nucleotide biosynthesis and purine metabolism. The phenotype spans a spectrum from neurodevelopmental delay, intellectual disability, dystonia, tremor, and other movement abnormalities, with variable expressivity and age of onset.

name: atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor, SHH-activated
definition: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of genes in the sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway (GLI2, BOC, PTCHD2, and MYCN).

name: atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor, MYC-activated
definition: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of the MYC gene.

name: atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor, TYR-activated
definition: An atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor characterized by overexpression of melanosomal genes (TYR, TYRP, MITF, and OTX2).

name: intracranial mesenchymal tumor, FET-CREB fusion-positive
synonyms: intracranial mesenchymal tumor with FET-CREB fusion
definition: A central nervous system mesenchymal non-meningothelial tumor with a broad morphological spectrum, characterized by fusion of a FET family gene (usually EWSR1 and rarely FUS) with a member of the CREB family of transcription factors (CREB1, ATF1, or CREM). It includes entities previously termed intracranial angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma or intracranial myxoid mesenchymal tumor. It is usually located in the supratentorial brain and mostly affects children and young adults. There is a spectrum of clinical behaviors ranging from slowly growing tumors to rapid recurrences, and rarely metastases.
parents: central nervous system mesenchymal non-meningothelial tumor

name: desmoplastic myxoid tumor of the pineal region, SMARCB1-mutant
definition: A pineal body neoplasm that is a SMARCB1-deficient tumor of the brain, characterized by the presence of spindled and epithelioid cells with low-grade morphology that are embedded in a desmoplastic stroma alternating with various extents of loose myxoid matrix.

name: cribriform neuroepithelial tumor
definition: A very rare, nonrhabdoid, intraventricular tumor with relatively favorable prognosis. It is characterized by the presence of neuroepithelial cells forming cribriform patterns, trabeculae, epithelial membrane antigen immunopositivity on epithelial surfaces, and loss of nuclear INI1 expression.

name: low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
definition: An ovarian serous carcinoma characterized by low-grade cytologic features, infrequent mitotic figures and slow tumor growth, which is thought to develop from a serous borderline ovarian tumor. It shows an activated mitogen-activated protein kinase pathway with KRAS and BRAF mutations and only rarely TP53 mutations, and is a distinct entity from high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma rather than a grade of it. It accounts for 2-5% of ovarian carcinomas and 5-10% of serous ovarian carcinomas.

name: tetrahydrobiopterin-unresponsive phenylketonuria
definition: A phenylketonuria in which blood phenylalanine concentrations do not fall substantially (conventionally defined as a reduction of more than 30%) in response to an oral tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4; sapropterin dihydrochloride) loading test, so that treatment with BH4 is not effective and phenylalanine-restricted dietary management remains necessary.

name: phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency
definition: A disorder of phenylalanine metabolism caused by biallelic variants in the PAH gene, encompassing the full spectrum of phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency from mild hyperphenylalaninemia, which requires no treatment, to phenylketonuria, in which untreated blood phenylalanine concentrations warrant phenylalanine-restricted dietary treatment.
grandparents: inborn disorder of phenylalanine and tyrosine metabolism

name: juvenile ossifying fibroma
definition: An ossifying fibroma arising predominantly in children and young adults, comprising two histological variants: juvenile trabecular ossifying fibroma and psammomatoid ossifying fibroma.

name: juvenile trabecular ossifying fibroma
definition: A juvenile ossifying fibroma predominantly arises in children and adolescents. It is characterized by prominent osteoid formation rimmed by osteoblasts in a fibrotic stroma. Patients usually present with painless jaw expansion that is associated with rapid growth and tooth displacement.

name: psammomatoid ossifying fibroma
definition: A juvenile ossifying fibroma arises usually affects individuals in their second to fourth decades with no sex predilection. It is characterized by the presence of multiple ossicles resembling psammoma bodies in a hypercellular stroma.

name: SMARCB1-related tumor predisposition
definition: Hereditary tumor predisposition due to variation(s) in the SMARCB1 gene. Pathogenic germline loss-of-function variants confer autosomal dominant predisposition to schwannomas, meningiomas, rhabdoid tumors and other rare types of tumors. The phenotype correlates with the variant's degree of loss of function: the schwannomatosis phenotype is more commonly observed with partial loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants, while the rhabdoid tumor phenotype is more commonly associated with complete loss-of-function variants.

name: severe chronic neutropenia
definition: A neutropenia characterized by persistent absolute neutrophil count below 0.5 x 10^9/L lasting for at least 3 months, not explained by medication use, infection or another underlying condition, and associated with recurrent and potentially life-threatening bacterial infections. The major clinical subtypes include congenital, cyclic, idiopathic, and autoimmune neutropenia, which share common diagnostic evaluation, treatment strategies, and long-term follow-up.

name: severe idiopathic neutropenia
definition: An idiopathic form of severe chronic neutropenia that cannot be classified as congenital, cyclic or autoimmune neutropenia, and is not explained by drug exposure, bone marrow failure, malignancy or systemic autoimmune disease. Symptoms are usually less severe than in congenital neutropenia, but infections can be life-threatening in some patients.

name: severe autoimmune neutropenia
definition: An autoimmune form of severe chronic neutropenia in which neutrophil-specific antibodies increase the destruction of circulating neutrophils, in the absence of systemic autoimmune disease. It is most common in children aged 6 months to 4 years, and it can also occur in adults. Serious bacterial infections are infrequent.

name: fibrous dysplasia/McCune-Albright syndrome
definition: A skeletal system disorder caused by a variation in the GNAS gene, characterized by involvement of the skin, skeleton and certain endocrine organs. Fibrous dysplasia ranges from an isolated monostotic lesion to severe polyostotic disease. McCune-Albright syndrome is diagnosed when fibrous dysplasia occurs with at least one extra-skeletal feature, or when two or more extra-skeletal features occur alone. The condition is not inherited. The signs and symptoms associated with the disorder vary greatly from person to person, depending upon the specific body cells and tissues that are affected by the gene variant.

name: posterior ischemic optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder characterized by ischemic injury to the retrobulbar (posterior) portion of the optic nerve, presenting with sudden visual loss and an initially normal-appearing optic disc, in contrast to anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. It may be arteritic (due to giant cell arteritis), nonarteritic, or surgical (following a surgical procedure).

name: traumatic optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder caused by closed or penetrating trauma to the face or head that injures the optic nerve, resulting in visual loss, often with an afferent pupillary defect.

name: radiation-induced optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder caused by radiation necrosis of the anterior visual pathway, occurring as a late complication of radiotherapy for head and neck or intracranial tumours and resulting in acute, painless and usually irreversible visual loss. Onset is typically 10 to 20 months after treatment but ranges from 3 months to 9 years.

name: compressive optic neuropathy
definition: An optic nerve disorder caused by mechanical compression of the optic nerve or chiasm along its course, for example by orbital or intracranial tumours, sinus mucoceles or thyroid eye disease, resulting in progressive visual loss.

name: ophthalmic artery occlusion
definition: An ocular vascular disorder characterized by acute complete obstruction of the ophthalmic artery, a branch of the internal carotid artery, leading to severe ischemia of the globe and associated ocular tissues. It can resemble central retinal artery occlusion with additional choroidal ischemia, and may cause sudden and permanent visual loss.

name: vitreomacular traction syndrome
definition: A vitreous and retinal disorder characterized by incomplete posterior vitreous detachment with persistent focal adhesion to the macula. This exerts anteroposterior traction that distorts foveal anatomy, causing structural changes such as foveal deformation, pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid, with potential progression to a macular hole.

name: traumatic macular hole
definition: A full-thickness macular hole that results from trauma, such as closed-globe or open-globe ocular injury, laser injury, surgical trauma, lightning strike or electrical shock. It occurs more often in young men, whereas idiopathic macular hole occurs more often in women older than 65 years.

name: juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis
definition: A uveitis occurring in individuals with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and its most frequent extra-articular manifestation. The most common form is chronic anterior uveitis, which is almost always asymptomatic in the initial stages, so screening of at-risk patients is essential.

name: secondary glaucoma
definition: A glaucoma in which elevation of intraocular pressure results from an identifiable pathophysiological mechanism, such as intraocular inflammation, pigment dispersion, hemorrhage, trauma, corticosteroid use or elevated episcleral venous pressure, in contrast to primary glaucoma. Secondary glaucomas form a heterogeneous group of diseases.
children_sample: glaucoma with elevated episcleral venous pressure

name: pigmentary glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma that can develop in pigment dispersion syndrome, in which pigment released from the iris is deposited in the trabecular meshwork, reducing aqueous outflow and raising intraocular pressure, leading to glaucomatous optic neuropathy. It is usually diagnosed between 40 and 50 years of age and occurs more often in men.

name: uveitic glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma in which optic nerve damage results from elevated intraocular pressure secondary to intraocular inflammation via trabecular inflammation/obstruction, steroid response, or synechial angle\nclosure in the setting of uveitis. Compared with primary open-angle glaucoma, it often has a more aggressive course, with very high intraocular pressure that waxes and wanes.

name: ghost cell glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma in which degenerated red blood cells (ghost cells), formed in the vitreous cavity after hemorrhage, pass forward into the anterior chamber and obstruct the aqueous outflow channels.

name: hemolytic glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma following intraocular hemorrhage, in which the trabecular meshwork is obstructed by fragments of hemolyzed red blood cells and hemoglobin-laden macrophages.

name: aniridia-associated glaucoma
definition: A secondary glaucoma occurring in individuals with aniridia. Most affected eyes have open anterior chamber angles, and a minority have partial or complete angle closure.

name: plateau iris syndrome
definition: A form of primary angle-closure glaucoma caused by a large or anteriorly positioned ciliary body that leads to mechanical obstruction of the trabecular meshwork. It is most often found in young patients.

name: exfoliation glaucoma
definition: A secondary open-angle glaucoma that develops in individuals with exfoliation syndrome. Exfoliation syndrome is associated with raised intraocular pressure in up to 44% of patients, making it the most commonly identifiable cause of secondary open-angle glaucoma.

name: FBN1-related geleophysic and acromelic dysplasia
definition: Any skeletal dysplasia in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the FBN1 gene. This condition is characterized by short stature, delayed bone age, stiff joints, acromegaly, hip dysplasia, respiratory issues (including sleep apnea and asthma), short hands/feet, and facial anomalies (such as a long philtrum, bulbous nose, broad/depressed nasal bridge, thick lips, and elongation of the eyelashes).

name: CAMK2A-related neurodevelopmental disorder
definition: Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the CAMK2A gene.

name: NUS1-related disorder
definition: Any hereditary disease in which the cause of the disease is a variation in the NUS1 gene. Biallelic variants cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation. Heterozygous variants, including deletions, cause a complex neurological disorder with developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy including developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and progressive myoclonus epilepsy, and movement disorders including myoclonus, dystonia, ataxia, tremor and parkinsonism. Rare NUS1 variants have also been associated with Parkinson's disease.
grandparents: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism
children_sample: congenital disorder of glycosylation, type Iaa
intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 55, with seizures

name: human ABL1 deficiency syndrome
definition: A multiple congenital anomalies/dysmorphic syndrome caused by homozygous loss-of-function variants in the ABL1 gene. It is characterized by multiple congenital malformations (wormian skull bones and brachydactyly) and distinctive facial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, prominent eyes, short, broad and flat nose, and macrostomia). It is allelic to, but clinically distinct from, congenital heart defects and skeletal malformations syndrome, which is caused by germline gain-of-function variants in ABL1.
grandparents: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism

name: TUBB-related tubulinopathy
definition: Any tubulinopathy in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TUBB gene. Heterozygous TUBB variants cause two overlapping developmental disorders, complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations (CDCBM) and congenital symmetric circumferential skin creases (CSCSC), also known as circumferential skin creases Kunze type. The clinical findings are diverse and include abnormalities of the cortex, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, brain stem and cerebellum, microcephaly, intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, excess skin folding and growth retardation.
children_sample: complex cortical dysplasia with other brain malformations 6

name: Gianotti-Crosti syndrome
definition: An acrodermatitis characterized by the acute onset of a self-limited, symmetrical, monomorphic papular or papulovesicular eruption predominantly on the cheeks, buttocks and extensor surfaces of the extremities, with relative sparing of the trunk. It mainly affects children between 1 and 6 years of age and is considered an immunologic reaction triggered by viral infections, most commonly Epstein-Barr virus and hepatitis B virus, or occasionally by vaccination. Lesions typically resolve spontaneously within weeks without scarring.

name: polymorphous adenocarcinoma
definition: A salivary gland adenocarcinoma that arises predominantly from the minor salivary glands, most often in the palate, and rarely from the major salivary glands. It is characterized by cytologic uniformity and architectural diversity, with tumor cells showing pale to clear nuclei with inconspicuous nucleoli arranged in a wide variety of growth patterns. It commonly harbors a PRKD1 E710D mutation, typically presents as a painless, slow-growing mass, and generally has an excellent prognosis.

name: avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder
definition: An eating disorder characterized by avoidance or restriction of food intake due to one or more of the following: lack of interest in eating or food, sensitivity to sensory characteristics of food (such as taste, texture, smell, or appearance), or concern about aversive consequences of eating (such as choking or vomiting), resulting in persistent failure to meet appropriate nutritional and/or energy needs as manifested by significant weight loss, nutritional deficiency, dependence on enteral feeding or nutritional supplements, or marked interference with psychosocial functioning, and where the eating disturbance is not better explained by lack of available food, cultural or religious practices, another mental disorder, or a concurrent medical condition.

name: cystic fibrosis-related diabetes
definition: A form of diabetes mellitus unique to individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF), arising primarily from progressive fibrotic destruction of the pancreas leading to insulin deficiency, with additional contributions from insulin resistance. CFRD affects approximately 20% of adolescents and 40-50% of adults with CF. It shares features with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes but is a distinct clinical entity with its own diagnostic criteria and management guidelines.

name: CFTR-related disorder
definition: A disease associated with CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) dysfunction that does not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for cystic fibrosis (CF). CFTR-related disorders are characterized by clinical evidence of CFTR dysfunction limited to a single organ system, a sweat chloride concentration below the CF diagnostic threshold (typically less than 60 mmol/L), and CFTR genotypes that often include at least one variant not classified as CF-causing. Recognized CFTR-related disorders include congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD), acute recurrent or chronic pancreatitis, and disseminated bronchiectasis.
grandparents: disease of genetic or genomic mechanism
children_sample: congenital bilateral aplasia of vas deferens from CFTR mutation

name: cystic fibrosis-related liver disease
definition: A liver disorder that arises as a consequence of cystic fibrosis. Cystic fibrosis-related liver disease encompasses a spectrum of hepatobiliary abnormalities caused by CFTR dysfunction in cholangiocytes, including focal biliary cirrhosis, multilobular biliary cirrhosis, hepatic steatosis, and cholangiopathy. It is a significant cause of non-pulmonary morbidity and mortality in CF, affecting approximately 5-10% of CF patients.

name: disease by body system or component
definition: A grouping class for human diseases classified by the body system or anatomical component primarily affected.

name: hepatic fibrinogen storage disease
definition: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by hypofibrinogenemia and variable liver disease (ranging from asymptomatic transaminase elevation to cirrhosis), caused by variants in FGG that lead to retention of variant fibrinogen as eosinophilic inclusions within the hepatocellular endoplasmic reticulum.

name: classical-like Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
definition: An Ehlers-Danlos syndrome characterized by skin hyperextensibility with velvety skin texture and absence of atrophic scarring, generalized joint hypermobility with or without recurrent dislocations, and easily bruised skin or spontaneous.
children_sample: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome due to tenascin-X deficiency

name: kyphoscoliotic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
definition: A rare systemic disease for which two subtypes exist, either related to the gene PLOD1 or FKBP14, and for which the clinically overlapping characteristics include congenital muscle hypotonia, congenital or early-onset kyphoscoliosis (progressive or non-progressive), and generalized joint hypermobility with dislocations/subluxations (in particular of the shoulders, hips, and knees). Additional features which may occur in both subtypes are skin hyperextensibility, easy bruising of the skin, rupture/aneurysm of a medium-sized artery, osteopenia/osteoporosis, blue sclerae, umbilical or inguinal hernia, chest deformity, marfanoid habitus, talipes equinovarus, and refractive errors. Gene-specific features, with variable presentation, are additionally observed in each subtype.

name: Athabaskan brainstem dysgenesis syndrome
definition: A HOXA1-related syndrome characterized by horizontal gaze palsy, sensorineural deafness, central hypoventilation, developmental delay, and intellectual disability, described in persons of Athabaskan American Indian heritage. Swallowing dysfunction, vocal cord paralysis, facial paresis, seizures, internal carotid artery, and cardiac outflow tract anomalies may be additionally observed. No dysmorphic facial features are associated.

name: infectious discitis
definition: An infection of the intervertebral disk space.

name: staphylococcus discitis
definition: Discitis caused by infection with Staphylococcus.

name: escherichia coli discitis
definition: Discitis caused by infection with Escherichia coli.

name: streptococcus pneumoniae discitis
definition: Discitis caused by infection with Streptococcus pneumoniae.

name: salmonella discitis
definition: Discitis caused by infection with Salmonella.

name: fungal discitis
definition: Discitis caused by infection with fungi.

name: WHIM syndrome 1
definition: A congenital autosomal dominant immune deficiency characterized by abnormal retention of mature neutrophils in the bone marrow (myelokathexis) and occasional hypogammaglobulinemia, associated with an increased risk for bacterial infections and a susceptibility to human papillomavirus (HPV) induced lesions (cutaneous warts, genital dysplasia and invasive mucosal carcinoma).

name: Martsolf syndrome 1
definition: This syndrome is characterized by the association of intellectual deficit, congenital cataract, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

name: antiphospholipid syndrome
definition: A disorder caused by the presence of autoantibodies directed against phospholipids, causing a hypercoaguable state, which may result in blood clots, stroke, heart attack, and in women, significant pregnancy-related complications, including miscarriage and still birth. The syndrome is often associated with other autoimmune disorders, most commonly lupus erythematosus, and infections, including syphilis and Lyme disease.

definition: A form of chronic intestinal pseudoobstruction caused by a developmental failure of the enteric neurons to differentiate or migrate properly and manifests as a bowel obstruction.

definition: Autosomal dominant form of antiphospholipid syndrome.

definition: Any 46,XY complete gonadal dysgenesis in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the DHX37 gene.

name: benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
definition: Idiopathic recurrent vertigo associated with positional nystagmus. It is associated with a vestibular loss without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in labyrinthitis and vestibular neuronitis inflammation in the ear is not observed.

name: type 3 autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
definition: A rare, primary immunodeficiency. It is caused by a currently undetermined defect in the Fas-induced apoptosis pathway. No mutations in Fas, FASLG or CASP10 are detectable. Disruption of Fas-induced apoptosis impairs lymphocyte homeostasis and immune tolerance. Characteristic laboratory findings include an increase in circulating, double-negative (CD4-/CD8-) T cells in the setting of immune-mediated anemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia. Clinical signs present in childhood include fatigue, pallor, bruising, hepatosplenomegaly and chronic, non-malignant, non-infectious lymphadenopathy. The clinical course is influenced by a strong association with other autoimmune disorders and an increased risk for developing Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

name: autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome, type III caused by mutation in PRKCD
definition: Any autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the PRKCD gene.
